title: Arijit Sings, the Internet Swoons: “Leher,” Cocktail 2’s First Full Song, Is the Grown-Up Ballad the Franchise Needed
excerpt: Pritam, Arijit Singh and Amitabh Bhattacharya reunite for a sun-drenched Sicilian love song — and Shahid, Kriti and Rashmika have never looked more in their feelings.
body:
Midnight in Mumbai, and the internet did what it always does when Arijit Singh's voice meets a Pritam melody — it went quiet, then it went feral. **"Leher,"** the first full song from **Cocktail 2**, dropped on June 23, and within hours the comment sections had turned into the kind of collective swoon you only get when a film hands you exactly the ballad you were hoping for.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=eh_5uIWqh2M</youtube>


![Arijit Singh — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b7/Arijit_Singh_performance_at_Chandigarh_2025.jpg)


Here is the thing about a *Cocktail* song: the bar was set impossibly high in 2012. "Tum Hi Ho Bandhu," "Daaru Desi," "Second Hand Jawaani" — that soundtrack didn't just sell the film, it *was* the film for a whole generation of NRIs who learned the choreography at every sangeet from New Jersey to Hounslow. So when **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon** and **Rashmika Mandanna** stepped into Homi Adajania's revival, the music had a ghost to outrun. "Leher" doesn't try to outrun it. It does something smarter — it slows down and lets you feel something.



> **"And the music is the bridge: a "Leher" at a Toronto wedding next month will get the exact same scream "Tum Hi Ho Bandhu" got a decade ago."**


> "Leher" — sung by Arijit Singh, composed by Pritam, written by Amitabh Bhattacharya. The dream team, back in the same room.


![Tum Hi Ho Bandhu — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/5/5d/Cocktail_2012_poster.jpg)


That trio — **Pritam**, **Arijit Singh**, **Amitabh Bhattacharya** — is the most reliable hit-factory in Hindi film music, and they know it. The song is a swelling, oceanic romantic number (the title literally means "wave"), and the visual grammar matches: sun-drenched Sicilian coastline, that golden-hour glow Adajania's films wear like a signature, and three of Bollywood's most magnetic faces caught mid-longing. Shahid, leaner and more weathered than his chocolate-boy years, plays the ache beautifully. Kriti glows. And Rashmika — the pan-India phenomenon making her full Hindi-romance statement here — holds the frame with a softness that the South already knew about and the North is catching up to fast.

What makes "Leher" land is restraint. There's no item-number flash, no drop engineered for Reels (though, trust, it'll be all over them by the weekend). It's a grown-up love song for a film that's positioning itself as a grown-up love story — a Delhi chef in a sixteen-year live-in relationship, the comfortable arrangement that suddenly isn't so comfortable when a third person walks in. Arijit, predictably, sings it like he's confessing something he shouldn't. The man could make a grocery list sound like heartbreak.


![Homi Adajania — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/70/Homi_Adajania_-_Director.jpg)


The timing is shrewd. **Cocktail 2** has already had a genuinely strong theatrical run — it closed its opening weekend around ₹44 crore, giving Shahid his third-biggest opener ever, and crossed ₹50 crore worldwide inside two days. A romance built on chemistry needs its love song to do the heavy lifting in week two, when the curiosity-buyers fade and the repeat-viewers and the date-night crowd take over. "Leher" is that lifting. It's the song couples will book tickets *for*.

For the diaspora, this is comfort food with a fresh coat of paint. The original *Cocktail* was practically a documentary about young Indians abroad — London flatshares, the push-pull between the wild girl and the good girl, the homesick ache underneath the parties. Part two relocates the fantasy to Italy, but the emotional postcode is the same. And the music is the bridge: a "Leher" at a Toronto wedding next month will get the exact same scream "Tum Hi Ho Bandhu" got a decade ago.

The film is in cinemas now, including across the US (where it carries an "A"-equivalent certificate overseas), the UK and Canada, with the full **Pritam** soundtrack streaming on the usual platforms. Universal Music is rolling the songs out one at a time — a slow drip designed to keep the album in conversation through the film's theatrical legs and, eventually, its OTT landing.

Is "Leher" a forever-classic on the level of the 2012 originals? Too early to crown it. Those songs had fourteen years to embed themselves in our nervous systems. But as a first full reveal, it's exactly what it needed to be — gorgeous, grown-up, and sung by the one voice that can still stop the timeline cold. The Adajania-Pritam-Arijit machine knows precisely what it's doing.

Pour another. This cocktail's still got notes left to reveal.
